text:
maya: Heads up — I'm seeing a 10-15% tail latency regression on llm-mistral-8x when sequences exceed ~4k. Repro script attached in the gist. Profiling points to a lot more memcpy activity in the KV copy path during decode. Suspect RoPE scaling / head-kv dim mismatch introduced by recent conversion update. :eyes:

liam: Can you paste the perf/top sample or a pprof flame? Also which kernel path was selected (fast-kv vs generic)?

maya: quick paste from perf top while decoding a 6k sequence:
```
  45.2%  inference_server  [kernel.kv_copy] 
  18.7%  inference_server  aten::layer_norm
  12.3%  inference_server  cudaMemcpy
```
Also runtime selected `kv_copy_opt_v2` on that model.

anita: Did we parse the HF config from the safetensors correctly? We've seen the conversion script drop rotary/scale metadata before. If head*head_dim != kv_dim * num_kv_heads pattern is off we get extra reshapes/copies.

ryan: Confirmed — the old conversion (`scripts/convert_hf_to_ri.py`) had a branch that normalized attention metadata and dropped `rotary_scaling` if it was nested under `attention` in older HF configs. Example HF snippet that caused trouble:
```json
{
  "num_attention_heads": 32,
  "attention": {
    "head_dim": 64
  }
}
```
After conversion we ended up with num_heads=32, head_dim=64 but no explicit `rotary_scaling` so the runtime picks a default that doesn't match the model's safetensors KV layout.

liam: That explains the memcpy. If runtime thinks kv_head_dim != actual layout it will do an explicit reorder. Two paths to mitigate: 1) force kernel selector flag `--force-kernel=kv-no-reorder` for this model as a short term, or 2) fix conversion + add a lint that verifies `num_attention_heads * head_dim == kv_dim * kv_heads` (or equivalent) during onboarding.

maya: I tried forcing the kernel with `--force-kernel=kv-no-reorder` locally. Latency drops back to baseline (roughly -12%) but it's a bit hacky. Batching heuristics also regressed: the continuous-batcher splits batches differently for >4k and that amplifies the cost.

anita: Agreed — permanent fix should be on the model metadata side. Ryan, can you update the conversion script to preserve `rotary_scaling` (and/or compute an explicit `kv_dim`) and add a unit test using the failing HF snapshot?

ryan: On it. I'll: 
- update convert_hf_to_ri to copy through rotary/scaling fields if present, falling back to computing kv_dim = num_attention_heads * head_dim if needed.
- add a regression test in tests/onboarding/ that runs a mini decode and asserts no reorder path chosen.
PR target: tomorrow morning.

ci-bot: label added: `oncall` `perf-regression` :hammer:

liam: Also let's add a runtime warning when parity check fails during model load: log a one-liner with suggested fix and a link to onboarding docs. That'll reduce time-to-diagnosis for next time.

maya: Thanks — I'll open the runtime lint issue and add the failing model to the smoke-test matrix once Ryan's PR lands. For immediate rollout I'll push a per-model config with `--force-kernel=kv-no-reorder` behind a canary and monitor.

anita: Nice. Also add a safetensors metadata sanity check to the conversion CI so we catch nested/missing fields early (fail fast).

ryan: Assigning self to conversion PR and test. Will reference this thread in the PR body.

maya: Action items summarized: 
- ryan: conversion + test PR (owner)
- liam: small runtime warning + docs link (owner)
- maya: canary with kernel override + monitor perf dashboard (owner)
- anita: add conversion CI check (owner)

maya: Thanks team — keeping this pinned until the fixes land. :thumbsup:
